summary.title: Tips for Self-Learning Programming
summary.one_liner: Practical advice for learning programming on your own: alternate reading and coding daily, get unstuck quickly by asking for help, build side projects, aim for "80% perfect," talk with other programmers, and revisit hard topics later.
takeaways: Alternate reading about code with writing code every day rather than in weekly or monthly blocks.
Don't stay stuck for more than about an hour; read the docs, search online (e.g., Stack Overflow), or ask someone.
Build your own side projects that interest you and that you can articulate how to implement.
Balance deep dives with pragmatic hacking; aiming for about 80% perfect is a reasonable target.
Talk with other programmers and revisit tools you struggled with months later.
summary.summary: This personal blog post by Jorge Silva gives a set of informal tips for someone teaching themselves programming, drawn from the author's own experience learning in college. It opens by discussing how to learn quickly sustainably, suggesting immersion, a mentor, or a group of beginners. The main body lists six tips: alternate reading and coding daily, avoid getting stuck and ask for help, work on side projects, balance perfectionism with hacking, talk to other programmers, and revisit difficult topics after time has passed. The post is anecdotal rather than a structured tutorial, and it recommends lobste.rs and Hacker News for reading.
